actions.action: Commit deduplication and the business update together
actions.mechanism: A unique event receipt and the business mutation share one transaction; acknowledge only after successful commit.
actions.implementation: Insert (partner, event_id) under a unique key. Only the inserting transaction may update business state. On duplicate, skip mutation and acknowledge.
actions.check: Crash before commit, after commit before acknowledgement, and during acknowledgement; replay concurrently. Verify exactly one committed business mutation.
actions.risk: External side effects require separate durable delivery handling.

actions.action: Fence entity updates with durable revision checks
actions.mechanism: An atomic revision comparison prevents older or equal revisions from changing newer entity state, independently of receipt retention.
actions.implementation: Within the receipt transaction, conditionally update only when incoming_revision exceeds stored_revision. Record stale events as processed. Preserve revision fences through entity deletion.
actions.check: Deliver revisions 12, 10, and 12 under different event IDs and concurrently; final revision remains 12 without repeated mutation.
actions.risk: For incremental deltas, buffer revision gaps instead of skipping missing updates.

actions.action: Expire receipts conservatively within a measured storage budget
actions.mechanism: First-receipt retention covers redelivery; strict expiry preserves the exact seven-day boundary without extending retention on duplicates.
actions.implementation: Retain receipts through first_received_at plus seven days; delete only afterward. Measure total table/index storage at one million receipts, including cleanup lag; backpressure before 2 GB.
actions.check: Replay just before and exactly at expiry: no mutation. After cleanup, replay an old revision: fence rejects it. Load-test storage stays below 2 GB.
actions.risk: Clock jumps, cleanup lag, and database bloat need monitoring; never evict unexpired receipts.
